items.text: LPBS already has a `requireAdminOrService()` middleware that accepts EITHER admin session cookies OR Bearer tokens (via LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET env var / .vrooli/secrets.json). Currently only used on remote-profiles and download-artifacts endpoints. Most admin endpoints (metrics/summary, admin/usage, admin/users, admin/coupons/usage) use `requireAdmin()` only. Widening these to `requireAdminOrService()` is a one-line change per route in LPBS routes.go — no new auth infrastructure needed.

Full API response shapes documented for all sources: (1) LPBS metrics/summary returns AnalyticsSummary with VariantStats array (views, CTA clicks, conversions, scroll depth). (2) LPBS admin/users returns paginated UsersListResponse with SubscriptionInfo and CreditInfo per user. (3) LPBS admin/usage returns UsageRecord array with user_totals and app_totals maps. (4) Swarm Manager /stats returns StatsResponse with 7 stat categories (throughput, timing, scope, blocking, agent, dashboard, review). (5) Swarm Manager /overview returns all backlog items, initiatives with rollup, dependency graph, summary, and governance. (6) Vrooli Core /scenarios returns scenario array with health_status and system_warnings. (7) Completeness-scoring /scores returns scenario scores with degradation info for partial/failed calculations.

Swarm Manager /overview does a FULL LOAD per request — all backlog items + initiatives + dependency graph. For a mature backlog this could be 10-50KB+ of JSON. Caching this in memory at 30s TTL is fine for a single-instance service, but the cache entry should use the raw JSON bytes (not deserialized structs) to minimize GC pressure. Alternatively, command-center can request only /stats for most dashboard views and reserve /overview for the Forge page.

Completeness-scoring API has built-in graceful degradation: partial results include confidence scores and missing_collectors lists, skipped scenarios report error and reason. Command-center can pass through the degradation info directly to the UI rather than building its own error handling for this source.

items.context: Command-center needs to call ~6 LPBS admin endpoints. LPBS already has requireAdminOrService() middleware (Bearer token via LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET) but it's only applied to 2 endpoint groups. The existing admin endpoints use requireAdmin() (session-cookie only).

options.label: Widen existing requireAdminOrService() to all admin endpoints command-center needs
options.rationale: Minimal LPBS code change — swap middleware on ~6 routes. Reuses existing Bearer token infrastructure. No new auth concepts. Other services can also use the same token.

options.label: Create new /api/v1/internal/* endpoints on LPBS with no auth (localhost-only)
options.rationale: Clean separation between browser-facing admin and service-to-service. But adds route duplication and a new auth pattern (network-level trust).

items.context: Command-center needs to expose aggregated data to its UI. Two design approaches: per-dashboard endpoints (one call per page) vs. per-source endpoints (UI composes from multiple calls).

options.label: Per-dashboard endpoints: GET /api/v1/dashboard/mission-control, /dashboard/hive, /dashboard/forge, etc.
options.rationale: Single request per page load. Backend composes exactly what each dashboard needs. Easier UI code. But tighter coupling — adding a widget to a dashboard requires backend change.

options.label: Per-source endpoints: GET /api/v1/sources/lpbs, /sources/swarm, /sources/scenarios
options.rationale: Loose coupling — UI composes freely. Fewer backend endpoints. But multiple requests per page, and UI needs to know which source has which data.

options.label: Hybrid: per-dashboard endpoints that internally delegate to per-source fetchers, plus a /sources/* escape hatch for custom views
options.rationale: Best of both — clean per-page API for known dashboards, flexible source access for ad-hoc needs. More code to maintain.

items.topic: New LPBS endpoint specifications for missing aggregations
items.context: Round 1 decided LPBS should compute derived metrics (MRR, churn, ARPU). Need to define what new endpoints LPBS should expose. Based on investigation, the missing aggregations are: revenue metrics (MRR/ARR by tier, churn rate, ARPU), subscription distribution (counts by tier × status with trends), and user growth (registration/active trends over time windows).

options.label: Three new endpoints: GET /api/v1/admin/revenue-summary, GET /api/v1/admin/subscription-stats, GET /api/v1/admin/user-growth
options.rationale: Clean separation by domain. Revenue summary: MRR, ARR, ARPU, churn rate, revenue by type. Subscription stats: counts by tier × status, trend arrays. User growth: registration and active user counts over 7/30/90-day windows.

options.label: Single comprehensive endpoint: GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard-summary that returns all aggregations
options.rationale: One call gets everything. Simpler for command-center. But large response and harder to cache selectively.

plan_updates: Updated conclusion with settled decisions from round 1 (API-first access, LPBS computes derived metrics, in-memory TTL cache). Added detailed findings on LPBS auth mechanism, full API response shapes, Swarm Manager memory considerations, and completeness-scoring degradation handling. New decisions focus on auth strategy, endpoint structure, and new LPBS endpoint specifications.
